title: Hot Baths May Help Your Heart, Study Finds
paragraphs: What's better than a nice hot bath after a long day? You can lie back, close your eyes and forget about your problems.
But a new study suggests that a hot bath might do more than help you relax — it could also be good for your heart!
Scientists from the University of Western Australia wanted to find out how hot baths affect the body, and how this compares with exercise.
They asked 25 overweight adults between the ages of 45 and 70 to take part in their study.
Participants spent 30 minutes sitting in hot water at 40 degrees Celsius, and 30 minutes riding an exercise bike.
The scientists checked what happened to participants' bodies during both activities, looking at things such as blood pressure and blood flow.

They found that when people sat in hot water, blood moved more easily through the small blood vessels under their skin. This happened because the heat made these blood vessels wider, giving the blood more room to move.
But after exercise, there was almost no change in how wide people's blood vessels were, or how well their blood moved.
The bath also lowered blood pressure much more than cycling did.
So, does this mean we can stop exercising and spend all day in the bath?

As nice as that sounds, hot baths aren't a replacement for regular exercise. The study only looked at what happened after one 30-minute bath or one 30-minute bike ride. It didn't show whether regular hot baths have the same long-term health benefits as exercise.
However, the findings suggest that hot baths might offer some benefits for people who find exercise difficult.
So the next time you enjoy a hot bath, remember that you're not just having a nice rest — you might also be doing something good for your heart!
